title: The intern screen now runs before anyone reads your résumé
angle: Automated coding assessments now gate applications before human review, so the résumé is no longer the first test; how a second-year student should reorder their preparation.
why_now: Summer 2027 cycle reports describe OAs sent before résumé review and assessments redesigned around AI use.
experience_hook: The writer's own Summer 2027 application season and the gap between advice that sounds productive and what moves an application forward.

title: What a payments internship teaches you that a LeetCode streak cannot
angle: Argue that owning one boring, money-touching system (retries, refunds, reconciliation) is stronger interview evidence than more solved problems, as interviews shift towards project reasoning.
why_now: Reporting in 2026 describes SWE interviews moving from memorised algorithm drills towards project reasoning and workflow evidence.
experience_hook: The writer's part-time payments engineering work and how they now describe it to recruiters.

title: AI makes my coding homework faster and my exams harder
niche: CS student life and study systems
angle: Studies show AI raises task scores without clear learning gains and makes debugging AI code harder under exam conditions; what a student's study system should change in response.
why_now: 2026 research and an educator survey report widespread exam redesign towards oral defences and proctored tests.
experience_hook: The writer's current semester of data structures, OS and linear algebra exams, and how their own study habits shifted.

title: Idempotency keys are a promise, not a header
angle: Explain idempotency through the failures it prevents (client retries, double charges) and the design decisions people skip: key scope, storage lifetime, and what to return on replay.
why_now: Idempotency-first payment design is a recurring 2026 topic in engineering blogs and system design prep, mostly shallow interview-style coverage.
experience_hook: Hands-on payments work and the lesson that plans which look sensible on a whiteboard fail under real retries.

title: Applying in November for a summer internship is not too late, but it is different
angle: Separate what is genuinely closed by late autumn (early FAANG waves, return offers) from what is still open, and how to pick targets instead of mass-applying.
why_now: Guides note many slots are filled by November through return offers, while rolling recruiting continues; students are anxious right now.
experience_hook: Building a tracked, systematic internship hunt rather than reacting to job-board noise.

title: Reconciliation is the test suite your payments system runs on production
angle: Reframe reconciliation from an accounting chore into an engineering safety net that catches what unit tests cannot, with the trade-offs of hourly versus daily checks.
why_now: 2026 write-ups treat reconciliation as an external safety net and describe varying cadences; a ledger-design piece is already trending in the fintech tag, so the adjacent topic has demand.
experience_hook: Payments engineering experience plus the writer's habit of asking what makes the rest unnecessary.

title: Why your payout bug is probably a units bug
angle: Many money bugs come from mixing cents and dollars, rounding at the wrong layer, or metering in one unit and paying in another; a checklist for catching them before finance does.
why_now: Payments system design content is popular, but most of it skips the mundane unit and rounding errors that cause real incidents.
experience_hook: First-hand auditing of payout and metering code, with specifics supplied by the writer.

title: How to talk about using AI in a coding interview without sounding like you cheated
angle: A practical stance on disclosing and explaining AI use in take-homes and project walkthroughs: show the judgement, not the output.
why_now: Companies are redesigning intern assessments around AI use and asking about AI fluency explicitly.
experience_hook: Contrasting viewpoints the writer favours: the popular answer (hide it), the tempting answer (lean on it), and the one that holds up.

title: Turn the AI off on purpose: a study rule that works
niche: CS student life and study systems
angle: Borrow the Berkeley finding that students deliberately switch AI off for some tasks and turn it into a concrete rule: which tasks to protect from AI and why.
why_now: Fresh research on students treating AI as a learning partner versus a shortcut, during final-exam season.
experience_hook: Lessons from building habits and discovering why sensible-looking plans fail in real life.

title: Webhooks lie by omission: designing for the event that never arrives
angle: Treat payment-provider webhooks as hints, not truth; how to combine them with polling, ordering checks and reconciliation so a missed event does not become a missed payout.
why_now: Webhook handling appears in nearly every 2026 Stripe-style system design guide but usually as a single bullet.
experience_hook: Real integration work with a payments provider in sandbox and production-like settings.

title: Studying for five finals at once without a colour-coded plan
niche: CS student life and study systems
angle: Argue against elaborate study schedules; the useful move is ranking courses by marks-at-risk per hour and cutting the rest.
why_now: End-of-term finals season; the students tag is full of generic study listicles with no point of view.
experience_hook: The writer's own overlapping November–December finals and the gap between looking productive and making progress.

title: If AI eats junior work, what should a second-year CS student practise?
niche: CS student life and study systems
angle: Take the 'broken junior pipeline' worry seriously and answer it with the skills that still compound: reading code, debugging, owning outcomes.
why_now: Industry discussion in 2026 that AI coding tools may be breaking the junior engineer pipeline.
experience_hook: Contrasting the popular, tempting and tested answers from the writer's own skill-building.

title: Group projects fail at the handoff, not the code
niche: CS student life and study systems
angle: Most student team projects break where work passes between people; lightweight habits borrowed from industry (issues, owners, definitions of done) that fix it.
why_now: End-of-semester group project crunch; little coverage that applies real engineering workflow to student teams.
experience_hook: Running several student team projects and hackathon entries as the de facto product owner.

title: The double-entry ledger, explained through one refund
angle: Follow a single refund through an append-only ledger with compensating entries, showing why you never edit a row and how balances are derived.
why_now: A double-entry ledger piece is trending across fintech, payments and architecture tags; a narrower, worked-example follow-up fills the gap.
experience_hook: Payments engineering work where refunds and payouts had to reconcile.

title: A spreadsheet beat every internship app I tried
angle: Why a plain tracker with a weekly review outperforms job-board apps for a focused internship hunt, and the few columns that matter.
why_now: Peak application season; community job lists for 2027 are huge and overwhelming.
experience_hook: The writer's own tracker-plus-playbook system for the Summer 2027 hunt.
